summary:
The instruction describes a single notification-dispatch service: one component that sends emails and in-app alerts for eight lifecycle events, gated on each event's toggle, with failures logged but non-blocking. That is server-side behaviour — sending mail, reading the toggle state at dispatch time, and logging the failure all happen in the backend repository, which is not checked out here.

I checked the one part of it that does belong to this repo — the Settings › Notifications surface that owns the toggle condition — and it is already built and wired to the real API:

- `src/services/settingsNotificationsService.js` calls `GET /api/v1/settings/notifications` and `PUT /api/v1/settings/notifications/{eventName}` exactly as the contract declares.
- `src/features/settings-admin/hooks/useNotificationEvents.js` / `useUpdateNotificationEvent.js` fetch and update toggles.
- `src/features/settings-admin/NotificationsTab.jsx` renders the event list from the API response (no inline event constants) with independent Email and In-App checkboxes, plus loading, empty, and error+retry states.
- `src/pages/SettingsAdminPage.jsx` mounts the tab behind the `TENANT_ADMIN` guard.

The event list itself comes from the backend's `GET /api/v1/settings/notifications` response, so the eight event names are not hard-coded here by design — adding them as frontend constants would violate the no-mock-data rule in CLAUDE.md.

I made no edits: every part of this instruction is either backend work or already true of this code.

Reading taken: I treated this as a backend dispatch-service request whose only frontend surface is the existing toggle condition, rather than as a request to add new UI.
blockers: The agent made no changes. The instruction may already be satisfied, or it may not map onto the code in this branch.

Not applied -- One service sends all emails and in-app alerts for approve, reject, send back, ready for signature, signing link, decline, executed, and new user invite: Belongs to the counterpart backend repository — email/in-app dispatch has no frontend surface, and stubbing it here would be fake work

Not applied -- Condition: the event's toggle must be ON in Settings > Notifications: Already true — NotificationsTab.jsx plus useNotificationEvents/useUpdateNotificationEvent are wired to GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/notifications; enforcing the condition at send time is backend
Not applied -- If the email fails: the action still completes and the failure is logged: Belongs to the counterpart backend repository — send-failure handling and logging happen server-side
